Weaviate is an open-source vector database (BSD-3) that meets the core requirement of being self-hostable via Docker or Kubernetes. 

**Key Findings:**
*   **Self-Hosting & Infrastructure:** It is fully self-hostable, though a high-availability (HA) deployment for our specific workload was estimated at approximately $60,000/year due to the infrastructure required by the K8s operator and the need for commercial tiers to access certain modules.
*   **Performance:** Internal benchmarks (primary data) show a p95 latency of ~15ms at 10M vectors with 96% recall.
*   **Features:** Its standout feature is built-in hybrid search (BM25 + vector), which significantly improves relevance for short queries.
*   **Operational Considerations:** It has the heaviest operational footprint among the candidates and introduces a GraphQL API, which may require a learning curve for the team.

data.content:
I have completed an in-depth investigation into your three vector database options: **pgvector**, **Qdrant**, and **Weaviate**. All three meet your primary requirement of being self-hostable and fall within your $100,000 annual budget.

### Synthesis & Comparison

| Feature | pgvector | Qdrant | Weaviate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Tech** | PostgreSQL Extension | Rust-based Engine | Open-source (BSD-3) |
| **Performance (p95)** | ~40ms @ 10M vectors | **~12ms** @ 10M vectors | ~15ms @ 10M vectors |
| **Key Advantage** | SQL familiarity & metadata filtering | Memory efficiency via quantization | Built-in Hybrid Search (BM25) |
| **Est. Annual Cost** | $12k - $18k | ~$30,000 | ~$60,000 (for HA setup) |

### Key Findings:

*   **pgvector:** This is the "safe" choice if your team is already proficient with PostgreSQL. It offers excellent integration for metadata filtering but has the highest latency among the three and lacks advanced quantization features.
*   **Qdrant:** This is the performance leader. Its Rust-based architecture provides the lowest p95 latency (12ms) and exceptional memory efficiency through binary quantization, which can reduce RAM requirements by up to 32x.
*   **Weaviate:** This is the "feature-rich" choice. While it has a higher operational footprint and cost for high availability, its built-in hybrid search (combining BM25 and vector) provides superior accuracy for short queries compared to the other two options.

### Recommendation:
*   Choose **Qdrant** if your primary drivers are **raw performance and infrastructure efficiency**.
*   Choose **Weaviate** if **search relevance (hybrid search)** is your top priority.
*   Choose **pgvector** if you want to leverage **existing SQL expertise** and a simpler operational model.
